Ashok Chandra: 
Good evening, ladies and gentlemen. First of all, I would like to touch upon the state of Indian 
economy. Indian economy continues to demonstrate a strong underlying growth momentum, 
supported by resilient domestic demand, infrastructure investment, expanding services activity, 
and a steadily strengthening financial system. 
 
India recorded real GDP growth of 7.8% in the first quarter of FY26-27 compared with 6.9% in 
the corresponding quarter of the previous year. Recently, MPC in its meeting and World Bank 
in its India Development report had also revised the GDP estimates for financial year FY26-27 
to 7.1% from the previous estimates of 6.7% and 6.6%, respectively. 
 
On the external front, India's Merchandise exports grew by 17.85% Y-o-Y during the period 
April to August 2026, reaching an estimated US$215.91 billion. The banking sector 
characterized by historically low levels of stressed assets and strong profitability is well 
positioned to play a pivotal role in supporting and sustaining India's economic expansion. 
 
Coming to Punjab National Bank, we sustained a strong business momentum in Q2, marked by 
a decisive improvement in margins in line with our expectations, continued strengthening of

asset quality and enhanced operating efficiency. Our performance reflects the strength of our 
franchise and disciplined execution of strategic priorities. We remain firmly on track to deliver 
our FY26-27 guidance. 
 
Our focus on retail, agriculture, and MSME continues to guide our efforts towards building a 
diversified and resilient advances book. At the beginning of the financial year, we have targeted 
to open 250 branches in this financial year with particular emphasis on strengthening our 
footprint in the Southern and Western regions. 
 
We have already opened 162 branches out of which 119 are in the Southern and Western region. 
In parallel, we are accelerating our digital transformation to build a more agile, efficient, and 
customer-centric organization. Our investments in technology, process automation and data 
analytics are aimed at simplifying banking journeys, improving service delivery, and enhancing 
productivity while positioning the bank to scale efficiency in a rapidly evolving banking 
environment. 
 
With this context, let me now turn to the segment-wise performance and key developments 
during the quarter. First, I will touch on the overall business growth. Our gross global business 
has reached INR  31.18 lakh crores, registering a robust Y-o-Y growth of 11.9%. 
 
Our advances grew by 14.7% Y-o-Y to INR  13.41 lakh crores despite reducing IBPC exposure 
by INR  23,700 crores. Excluding this impact, core advances registered a robust Y-o-Y growth 
of 17.4%, reflecting healthy credit demand and strong underlying business momentum. Our core 
RAM portfolio continued to deliver healthy growth with retail advances, excluding IBPC 
growing by 16.3%, MSME by 19.8%, and agriculture (priority sector) by 18.1% Y-o-Y, 
reflecting broad-based traction across key segments. 
Credit growth is well positioned to maintain its strong momentum, supported by a robust 
sanction pipeline. Bank sanctioned INR  4 lakh crores in FY 2025-26 in corporate credit lines. 
Further, in the first half of this year, we have already crossed more than INR  2.5 lakh crores of 
sanctions in the corporate credit. Our pipeline credit is to the tune of INR  1.58 lakh crores, 
which provides a strong visibility for future credit growth. 
Global deposits of the bank have reached to INR  17.77 lakh crores with Y-o-Y growth of 9.9%. 
Our CASA strategy is centered on deepening customer engagements and enhancing individual 
saving account balance, which grew by 8.1% Y-o-Y. In the beginning of FCNR campaign, we 
had targeted to raise USD 2.5 billion, and we have raised USD2.7 billion in a calibrated manner. 
The same has been utilized for shedding of our high-cost bulk deposits and CDs. With a CD 
ratio of  75.5%, we have adequate balance sheet headroom to support planned credit expansion. 
Accordingly, our deposit mobilization remains measured and strategic with a clear emphasis on 
optimizing the cost of funds rather than pursuing volume at any cost. 
I will touch upon the profitability. Improving profitability remains the bank's foremost strategic 
priority as consistently emphasized across various forums. As indicated in our previous 
interaction, we had expected a sequential improvement in margins during FY 2026-27. Our Q2

performance validates this assessment with a substantial improvement in margins during the 
quarter. 
Domestic NIM improved by 10 basis points sequentially from 2.64% to 2.74%, while global 
NIM increased from 2.5% to 2.58%. We expect this positive trajectory to strengthen further in 
the coming quarters, supported by disciplined balance sheet optimization. NII increased to INR  
11,601 crores, registering Y-o-Y growth of 10.8% and sequential growth of 7.4%, surpassing 
our stated guidance of 7%. 
Operating profit is continuously above INR  7,500 crores mark from the last 3 quarters and 
stands at INR 7,532 crores for Q2 of this year. Core operating profit, excluding recoveries from 
written-off accounts and treasury gains, grew by 29.4% Y-o-Y basis and 8% on a Q-o-Q basis. 
Core operating profit forms 79% of the total operating profit in Q2 of FY2027, which was 64% 
in Q2 of FY26. 
Our fee-based income grew by 16% on Y-o-Y basis, reflecting continued progress in 
diversifying revenue sources. The bank recorded a net profit of INR 5,532 crores in Q2 with Y-
o-Y growth of 12.8%. The bank's overall earnings profile reflects a sustained focus on profitable 
growth and strengthening core earnings. 
Efficiency ratios. Our return on assets has consistently remained above 1% mark and stands at 
1.05% in Q2 of this year. Our return on equity stands at 17.32%. Our tangible book value per 
share stood at INR 111.94 as on September 30, 2026, registering a significant improvement over 
INR 95.92 as on September 30, 2025. 
Our cost-to-income ratio has demonstrated a consistent declining trend, improving to 50.45% in 
Q2 from 51.20% in Q2 of last year, reflecting our continued focus on operational efficiency and 
cost optimization. I will touch upon the asset quality. 
Asset quality continues to strengthen with the gross NPA ratio declined to 2.55% as on 
September 30, 2026 from 3.45% as on 30th September 2026. The net NPA ratio has also 
improved to 0.25% as of September 30, 2026 from 0.36% as on 30th September 2025. This 
sustained improvement reflects our disciplined credit underwriting, robust monitoring, and 
focused recovery efforts while keeping us firmly on track to achieve our FY26-27 guidance on 
both GNPA and net NPA. 
We have not seen any material impact of geopolitical tensions on the bank's asset quality. Our 
slippages remain contained, SMA accounts are stable, and the overall credit portfolio continues 
to perform well. Our SMA-0, 1, and 2 all combined, is all-time low levels of 2.50% of the overall 
loan book. Our PCR stands at 97.32%, which is well above our guidance of more than 96% for 
FY’27. 
Total fresh slippages during the Q2 of this year is INR 2,395 crores and our guidance for 
slippages ratio to remain below 0.9% in FY’27. We are within our guidance level -- we are at 
0.77%. Total recovery stood at INR 2,805 crores for Q2 of this year, and our recovery is 1.17 
times of the slippages in Q2, reflecting our commitment towards improving asset quality. We

September 2026, almost 6.25 years, we have sanctioned around INR 15.97 lakh crore loans, out 
of which we have disbursed INR 14.09 lakh crores loans. And the outstanding in these loans is

September 2025. Our CET1 capital stands at 14.44% against regulatory requirement of 8%, Tier 
1 capital stands at 15.89% against regulatory requirement of 9.5%, including CCB and Tier 2

advance above INR 25 crores are above A-rated, and more than 52.4% are AAA-rated, which 
indicates our balance sheet strength from risk point of view. 
 
Our digital transformation is reshaping the bank into future-ready institution, driving superior 
customer experience, operational efficiency, and sustainable growth. Our H1 FY‘27, our digital 
sanction has crossed INR 41,500 crores, reflecting strong momentum towards our ambition of 
adding INR Ione more lakhs crores during this financial year. On the transaction side, over 95% 
of the customer transactions are now digital, and there is 31% Y-o-Y increase in digital 
transactions. We have further strengthened our digital payment offering by enabling UPI 
services for our current account customers through flagship product PNB One business mobile 
app. 
 
There is good traction in the PNB One business app, and this app caters to more than 4.14 lakhs 
customers with more than 225 features. We remain at the forefront of supporting RBI and 
government-led initiative in CBDC and digital public infrastructure. Going forward, we are 
expanding the application of AI and machine learning across operations, advanced analytics, 
risk management, and decision-making. Anchored in responsible AI practices, robust 
governance, and regulated compliance, this initiative will further enhance the bank's agility, 
productivity, and customer-centricity. 
 
PNB is taking steps towards becoming quantum-ready. We have deployed quantum-safe 
encryption in 246 of our customer-facing applications based on framework provided by NIST, 
USA. We are pioneering quantum technologies in banking through our Quantum Finance 
Innovation Hub at Amaravati, Andhra Pradesh, to advance cybersecurity, fraud detection, and 
secure digital financial services to strengthen the bank's technological resilience and future 
readiness. 
 
Now, I will touch upon the most important aspect, that is the human resource. We are investing 
in targeted capability building through customized certification program in collaboration with 
IIBF. Bank has launched a large-scale Artificial Intelligence Enablement Program with 
Microsoft, which has trained 47,545 officers of the bank. These initiatives have equipped our

bank has received Golden Peacock National Training Award for the year 2026. 
 
Through initiatives such as PNB SPARSH offering telecommunication support for mental well-
being, regular health checkups and wellness sessions, and childcare facilities, including creche 
services, we are fostering a supportive and inclusive workplace that prioritizes employees' 
physical, mental, and family well-being. Our pan-India initiative such as PNB Khel Utsav and 
PNB Taal Tarang provides platforms for employees to showcase their sporting and cultural 
talents, fostering a sense of belonging and promoting a vibrant organizational structure. 
 
Now, I will be concluding. The bank is sharpening its focus on profitability by strengthening its 
savings individual franchise and drive calibrated growth in the retail, agri, and MSME segments 
to enhance margins, optimize the cost of funds, improve business mix, and deliver sustainable 
growth in the earnings and returns ratio. 
 
Our robust risk management framework, anchored in prudent underwriting, disciplined credit 
monitoring, and focused recoveries, is strengthening asset quality and containing credit cost. 
Credit cards, cash management services, and supply chain finance are emerging as key drivers 
of diversified fee-based revenue growth. 
 
In parallel, the bank is expanding its growth avenues through the introduction of wealth 
management services and the comprehensive revamp of trade finance modules aimed at 
enhancing customer value, strengthening service delivery, and improving non-interest income.  
 
Anchored in a strong balance sheet, disciplined execution, and diversified growth drivers, the 
bank is well positioned to drive sustainable profitability, strengthening return ratios, and deliver 
consistent long-term values to stakeholders. Thank you very much, and I am open for any 
questions or any clarification related with the financial performance of our bank of Q2 financial 
year FY’26-27. Thank you.
